newsitem.title: UK: BT says agrees merger with MCI.
newsitem.headline: BT says agrees merger with MCI.

text.p: British Telecommunications Plc said on Sunday that it had agreed a merger with MCI Communications Corp, creating a telecoms giant with annual revenue of over 25 billion pounds ($41 billion).
The company told Reuters that the cash and shares deal included a 35p a per share special dividend.

The merged group, to be called Concert Plc, creates the world's second largest telecoms group and values MCI shares at 0.54 new Concert American Depositary Shares (ADRS) and $6.0 cash -- a total cash payment of up to $3.8 billion to MCI investors.

"The merger combines the substantial financial resources and global postition of BT with the growth momentum and market expertise of MCI, known for its success in the competitive U.S. long distance market," BT said in a later statement.

The new telecoms giant, incorporated in Britain, will have headquarters in London and Washington and operate under the BT and MCI brand names in Britain and the U.S. respectively. The deal is dependent on regulatory clearance.

BT, whose attempts to merge with British rival Cable and Wireless failed six months ago, said the deal would create a world leading communications power house with annual cash flow of about 7.5 billion pounds and 43 million business and residential customers in 70 countries.
